title: SLIN vs Insulin Herb Berberine: Serving & Formula Checks
question: Same ingredient, different serving?
description: Compare SLIN and Insulin Herb Berberine by serving size, disclosed formula and US order commitment. See why a shared berberine name does not establish equivalent products.
lead: SLIN and Insulin Herb Berberine both use berberine in their metabolic marketing, but the published amounts use different serving units and the linked orders differ. This comparison helps US adults read those differences before considering either product.

sections.title: Put the serving units beside the number
paragraphs: SLIN lists 500 mg berberine HCl per four-capsule manufacturer serving. The newly reviewed Insulin Herb panel lists 500 mg berberine HCl per one vegetarian capsule. These use the same named ingredient form but different serving denominators. They are not a personal dose-for-dose substitution, and a higher per-capsule amount does not establish a better result.

The Insulin Herb panel now resolves a gap in our earlier guide: it lists milk thistle seed extract 105 mg, standardized to at least 80% silymarin, and piperine 5 mg. SLIN presents a wider multi-botanical formula, but its separate affiliate bundle still mentions Gymnema, absent from the current manufacturer table. Neither list constitutes an independent assay.

sections.title: The bottle price does not describe the linked order
paragraphs: Our SLIN guide leads to a six-bottle offer. Its separate manufacturer store advertised US$45.99 for one bottle, which is a different purchasing route. Comparing that store figure with the affiliate bundle without naming the quantity would hide the larger upfront commitment.

The Insulin Herb guide records one- and three-bottle prices and conflicting shipping language. Its sales page describes a 30-day bottle while also using two-to-three-capsule directions. Treat those supply claims as unresolved arithmetic, not instructions to take two or three capsules. Request the actual bottle label and an address-specific quote.

sections.title: What to settle before choosing
paragraphs: Ask SLIN for the formula attached to the exact affiliate bundle and resolve whether Gymnema belongs to that version. For Insulin Herb, compare the newly available full panel with the physical package and its shared-equipment allergen warning. Both complete formulas, rather than just their berberine entry, belong in a suitability review.

Neither a product name nor seller copy justifies changing diabetes care or combining a supplement with a prescription medicine. Take the full ingredient lists to a qualified clinician or pharmacist. This article compares label transparency and order structure; it does not recommend a dose or claim a head-to-head clinical advantage.

verdict: The newly reviewed Insulin Herb panel supports a specific three-ingredient comparison, while SLIN offers a wider manufacturer formula with an affiliate-bundle discrepancy. The shared 500 mg headline uses different serving units. Neither ingredient count nor capsule concentration establishes a clinical winner.

sections.title: A nighttime claim does not identify the ingredients
paragraphs: The clearest distinction is the evidence available for composition. Elixolve publishes a defined strip serving and named amounts. The reviewed Gluconite materials do not establish a readable complete current Supplement Facts panel. That prevents a reliable ingredient-by-ingredient match.

Do not copy a melatonin amount from another marketplace or an older bottle with a similar name. The 1 mg figure belongs to the reviewed Elixolve strip label only. An oral strip also does not, by format alone, prove faster absorption or better sleep than another product.

sections.title: Count strips and bottles separately
paragraphs: Two Elixolve tins contain 60 strips. Three contain 90, and six contain 180. A Gluconite bottle is described commercially as a 30-day supply, but a confirmed quantitative serving is still needed before it can be compared on a per-serving basis. Bottle count and strip count are different measures.

The similar entry prices hide different quantities. Gluconite's single-bottle checkout recorded a shipping charge; Elixolve advertises free US shipping, without a complete address quote in the registered guide. Neither example establishes today's delivered cost for your address.

A longer period does not demonstrate product effectiveness or make a purchase risk-free. Confirm postage and which order terms govern. If sleep problems persist, seek qualified assessment rather than treating either seller's nighttime narrative as a diagnosis or a reason to change medication.

verdict: Elixolve supports a more specific serving comparison because the reviewed strip panel states amounts. Gluconite remains a full-label enquiry before an ingredient comparison can be completed. This is a transparency distinction, not a claim that one product improves sleep more.

title: SlimSana vs. KetoSana: Kapseln, Tropfen und Etiketten
question: Kapseln oder Tropfen?
description: SlimSana und KetoSana im Vergleich: Kapseln oder Tropfen, deklarierte Mengen, offene Etikettenfragen und Gesamtkosten. Keine Empfehlung zum Abnehmen oder zur Kombination.
lead: SlimSana und KetoSana werden für ähnliche Gewichts- und Stoffwechselinteressen angeboten. Für deutschsprachige Erwachsene ist der brauchbare Vergleich das konkrete Format, die verfügbare Deklaration und die Bestellung — nicht die Stärke der Werbeversprechen.
rows: 30 Kapseln; eine Kapsel als deklarierte Portion
100 µg Chrom und 85 mg Berberin-HCl pro Etikettenportion
Aktuelle vollständige Mengen pro Tropfenportion hier nicht bestätigt
Unter anderem 154 mg Grüntee-Extrakt und 150 mg Apfelessig

sections.title: Das Format ist eine Vorliebe, kein Wirksamkeitsbeleg
paragraphs: SlimSana erlaubt anhand seines verlinkten Etiketts eine konkrete Betrachtung einzelner Mengen. KetoSana beschreibt ein Tropfenformat. Ohne gleichwertige vollständige Angaben pro Portion lässt sich daraus jedoch kein seriöser Mengenvergleich berechnen. Eine Pipette ist keine automatisch standardisierte Vergleichseinheit.

Aussagen über besonders schnelle Aufnahme, Ketose oder eine Alternative zu verschreibungspflichtiger Behandlung werden hier nicht als nachgewiesen übernommen. Auch der Produktname KetoSana belegt nicht, dass das fertige Produkt einen bestimmten Stoffwechselzustand herstellt. Entscheidend sind aktuelle Deklaration und individuelle Eignung.

sections.title: Chrom und Pflanzenstoffe nicht als Rangliste lesen
paragraphs: Das SlimSana-Etikett nennt neben Chrom mehrere Pflanzenstoffe. Die Mengen verschiedener Extrakte sind keine untereinander austauschbaren Wirksamkeitspunkte. Bei KetoSana müssen zuerst die genaue Portion, Inhaltsstoffe, Mengen, Trägerstoffe und Warnhinweise der aktuellen Flasche geklärt werden.

Für SlimSana ist zudem eine abweichende Chrom-Referenzprozentangabe gegenüber einem anderen Sana-Etikett dokumentiert. Diese Prozentwerte werden nicht als Qualitätsmaßstab verwendet. Fragen Sie bei Unklarheiten nach dem aktuellen Etikett und lassen Sie die gesamte Kombination mit bestehenden Medikamenten prüfen.

sections.title: Was ein fairer Kostenvergleich benötigt
paragraphs: Der dokumentierte SlimSana-Produktpreis für einen Flakon beträgt 69 €. Seine Versandseite nennt 9 €, während ein unvollständig adressierter Checkout zunächst 0 € zeigte. Das ist kein endgültiges Lieferangebot. Für KetoSana wäre zusätzlich eine bestätigte Flüssigkeitsmenge und Portion nötig, bevor Kosten pro Portion sinnvoll berechnet werden können.

Klären Sie bei beiden Angeboten Lieferland, Steuer, Gesamtbetrag und Rückgabe für genau Ihre Bestellung. Der SlimSana-Ratgeber beschreibt 60 Tage ab Bestelldatum und Rückporto beim Kunden. Eine größere Vorratsbestellung oder die Kombination beider Produkte lässt sich weder aus einer ähnlichen Werbung noch aus einem niedrigeren Stückpreis ableiten.

verdict: Wer die Formate vergleicht, findet bei SlimSana ein quantitatives Kapseletikett und bei KetoSana weiterhin offene Fragen zur vollständigen Tropfendeklaration. Erst diese Angaben klären; aus dem Format allein folgt kein Vorteil für Gewichtsverlust.

Bei KetoSana Flüssigkeitsmenge und Portion bestätigen.

title: MetaboSana vs. GlucoSana: Mengen und Warnhinweise
question: Mengen und Warnhinweise vergleichen
description: MetaboSana und GlucoSana: gleiche Kapselzahl, unterschiedliche Nährstoffe und Warnhinweise. Vergleichen Sie Mengen, Grüntee-Angaben, Kurkuma und Bestellbedingungen.
lead: MetaboSana und GlucoSana sind Mehrstoff-Kapseln mit überlappender Stoffwechselwerbung. Beide geprüften Etiketten nennen 30 Kapseln, doch die Zusammensetzung und die hervorgehobenen Warnhinweise unterscheiden sich deutlich.
rows: 75 mg Alpha-Liponsäure; 75 mg Grünteeblatt; 5,5 mg Zink
90 mg Vitamin C; 25 µg Vitamin D; 200 mg Kurkuma-Rhizom

sections.title: Gleiche Berberinmenge bedeutet nicht gleiche Formel
paragraphs: Die beiden Etiketten nennen jeweils 50 mg Berberin-HCl pro Kapsel. Dieser gemeinsame Eintrag beschreibt nur einen Teil der Rezeptur. Unterschiedliche Mengen Chrom, andere Vitamine und zusätzliche Pflanzenstoffe müssen daneben gelesen werden. Eine einzelne Übereinstimmung beweist weder Austauschbarkeit noch gleiche Wirkung.

Auch die 200 mg Kurkuma-Rhizom bei GlucoSana sind nicht gleichbedeutend mit 200 mg isoliertem Curcumin. Bei MetaboSana beziehen sich die Prozentangaben für Polyphenole, Catechine und EGCG auf dieselbe Grüntee-Zutat. Sie werden weder als zusätzliche Zutaten addiert noch als klinische Ergebnisse ausgelegt.

sections.title: Warnhinweise entscheiden vor dem Preis
paragraphs: Das MetaboSana-Etikett warnt unter anderem vor zusätzlichem Grüntee am selben Tag und vor Einnahme auf nüchternen Magen. Seine genannte EGCG-Obergrenze ist keine Zielmenge oder persönliche Dosierungsempfehlung. Bei GlucoSana stehen andere, unter anderem kurkumabezogene Einschränkungen im Vordergrund.

Eine höhere Chrommenge oder die gleiche Kapselzahl macht kein Produkt automatisch geeigneter. Lassen Sie die vollständigen Etiketten zusammen mit Medikamenten und anderen Präparaten fachlich prüfen. Dieser Vergleich begründet keine Kombination beider Produkte und keinen Ersatz einer ärztlichen Behandlung.

sections.title: Gleicher Einstiegspreis, noch kein gleicher Lieferpreis
paragraphs: Für beide Angebote ist ein Produktpreis von 69 € pro Flasche dokumentiert. Die Versandtexte nennen bei einem Flakon 9 €, während nicht vollständig adressierte Checkouts zunächst 0 € zeigten. Ein solcher Anfangswert lässt sich nicht als verbindlicher Preis für Ihre Adresse übernehmen.

Die Richtlinien nennen 60 Tage, unterscheiden sich aber darin, wie klar der Fristbeginn festgelegt wird. Vor dem Kauf sind Bestelldatum beziehungsweise Fristbeginn, Rücksendeanweisung und das Rückporto zu klären. Ein identischer Preis und eine ähnliche Garantiezahl beseitigen die Unterschiede bei Zusammensetzung und Eignung nicht.

verdict: MetaboSana hebt Grüntee und Alpha-Liponsäure hervor; GlucoSana enthält eine andere Nährstoff- und Pflanzenkombination mit Kurkuma. Die sinnvolle Auswahl beginnt mit Warnhinweisen und der vollständigen Formel, nicht mit einem Mengen- oder Preisgewinner.

sections.title: Turmeric appears in both, in different formulations
paragraphs: Curcumitol-Q declares a named turmeric-root ingredient and quercetin. Advanced Joint Support lists a wider mixture, including a turmeric phytosome alongside glucosamine and several botanical ingredients. A shared reference to turmeric does not make these ingredient forms, serving sizes or finished products equivalent.

Curcumitol-Q's curcuminoid percentages describe its ingredient specification. They are not a clinical score and cannot establish superiority over the joint-support blend. Likewise, a greater ingredient count in Advanced Joint Support is not evidence of greater relief. We have not conducted a comparative trial.

sections.title: Resolve count and allergen questions before unit pricing
paragraphs: The Advanced Joint Support materials show a practical inconsistency: photographs state 60 tablets while the full label states 120, with four tablets per serving. Until the seller confirms which version ships, a cost-per-serving calculation would give a misleading appearance of precision.

Its glucosamine source is another concrete distinction: the displayed label identifies crab and/or shrimp. That matters to a label discussion with a qualified professional, especially for shellfish allergy. The narrower Curcumitol-Q composition is still not a guarantee of suitability or freedom from interactions.

sections.title: Compare the same destination and pack commitment
paragraphs: The linked Curcumitol-Q order uses six bottles; the linked Advanced Joint Support order uses three. The registered UK example for Joint Support included a US$29.95 shipping charge. Ask for each current full total in the same country, including shipping, possible import charges and currency conversion. Both registered guides describe a 90-day return period with customer-paid return postage, but order-specific instructions still apply. Persistent joint pain deserves assessment rather than a purchase decision based on testimonial strength.

verdict: Curcumitol-Q is the more focused formula by declared ingredient scope. Advanced Joint Support has a broader blend, a shellfish-source consideration and an unresolved tablet-count version. None of these observations establishes which product will relieve symptoms or work better.

sections.title: An amino-acid blend and an HMB formula answer different label questions
paragraphs: Advanced Amino Formula identifies eight amino acids and a combined 5,000 mg blend. The total does not reveal how much leucine or any other individual component is present. Advanced Muscle Plus separately declares dileucine and calcium HMB. These are different ingredient statements, not quantities to place on one scale and rank by total milligrams.

The calcium line on the Muscle Plus panel comes from its calcium HMB ingredient. Adding that calcium number to the HMB amount would double-count part of the same ingredient. Neither a larger combined weight nor more tablets establishes better strength or recovery.

sections.title: Read the vitamin D caution before choosing a pack
paragraphs: The displayed Muscle Plus label lists 200 µg vitamin D per six-tablet serving. NHS public guidance warns adults against taking more than 100 µg daily unless a doctor advises otherwise. The published entry is therefore a reason for individual medical review, not a routine dose recommendation or a printing error we can assume away.

Do not reduce tablets or create a new schedule to work around that warning based on this article. Ask a qualified clinician to assess the complete formula and all other sources of vitamin D. The absence of the same vitamin entry from the reviewed Amino Formula panel does not establish that the alternative is suitable for everyone.

sections.title: Price comparisons need matching quantities and delivery
paragraphs: The recorded one-bottle prices differ, but both products use 30 label servings per container, with different formulas. This supports a package-cost comparison only after suitability is settled. A lower cost per label serving is not a cost per unit of muscle gained.

The registered guides also open different packs and record different country-level shipping examples. Ask for matching quotes to the same address. Both guides describe a 90-day return period with customer-paid postage; the Muscle Plus materials also disagree about treatment of original shipping. Confirm the exact order conditions before paying.

verdict: Amino Formula is a combined amino-acid blend with undisclosed individual amounts. Muscle Plus separately lists dileucine, HMB and a vitamin D entry requiring medical review. The first decision is whether the formulation is appropriate, not which pack appears cheaper.

Memory Formula also declares a 150 mg phosphatidylserine complex from soy lecithin, 120 mg bacopa extract and 80 mg ginkgo, among other entries. It explicitly states Contains Soy. sections.title: Separate focus marketing from a memory assessment

Advanced Memory Formula now has a readable quantitative panel in this review, rather than only an eleven-ingredient narrative. That improves label comparison, but it is still not a clinical test of memory improvement. Seller ingredient citations and customer quotations do not establish a head-to-head advantage. Ask both sellers to confirm that the quantitative panel matches the exact current order, along with the quantity, eligible address and delivered total. verdict: Both supplier panels now support specific comparisons, but they use different Alpha-GPC ingredient strengths and capsule or tablet servings. Memory Formula also explicitly identifies soy. These distinctions help a label discussion; they do not identify a better product for focus or memory.

description: SenFlo Gummies and Integrative Digestive Formula use digestive marketing but have different ingredient types and missing-information limits. Compare purpose, serving evidence and delivery markets.
lead: SenFlo Gummies and Integrative Digestive Formula share a broad digestive-shopping category, but senna-based occasional use and a multi-blend capsule formula are different proposals. This comparison explains why their serving and purchase information cannot be treated as interchangeable.
rows: Vegetarian capsules; one capsule per label serving, 60 servings
Senna leaf extract; complete quantitative panel not established
Zinc 7.5 mg, chromium 100 µg and three separately stated blend totals
Senna or sennoside amount per serving needs confirmation
Botanical blend 450 mg; mushroom blend 60 mg; enzyme blend 52 mg
Complete ingredients, quantitative serving and warnings
Individual blend amounts and enzyme activity units are undisclosed
US$49 plus US$19.90 initial shipping, 26 October checkout
US$39.95 before destination charges, 7 October recorded offer
Registered offer lists UK; verify address rather than assuming US shipping terms

sections.title: Digestive is a category, not one mechanism or use pattern
paragraphs: SenFlo names senna, which NHS guidance identifies as a stimulant laxative. Integrative Digestive Formula instead presents botanical, mushroom and enzyme blends. A broad reference to digestive comfort does not establish the same purpose, strength or suitability for either product.

NHS guidance advises against senna use beyond seven days unless a doctor or pharmacist recommends it. That general advice does not verify these gummies' strength or provide a dosing schedule. It does show why the seller's 15-, 45- or 90-day package descriptions must not be read as recommendations for continuous use.

sections.title: Both products leave different quantitative questions open
paragraphs: For SenFlo, the missing full current Supplement Facts is the first obstacle. The front-bottle artwork and the word senna do not establish the amount per gummy or a complete warning list. Asking for the panel is more useful than trying to infer strength from a commercial supply-day claim.

Integrative Digestive Formula provides three blend totals, but not the individual botanical amounts or enzyme activity units. A milligram total of enzymes does not supply the missing activity information. The more detailed panel therefore improves some comparisons without resolving every clinical or ingredient question.

sections.title: Keep the two delivery markets separate
paragraphs: The SenFlo checkout recorded US$68.90 for one bottle including initial shipping, despite free-shipping language on the sales page. The Integrative price is a product-only reference from a UK-listed order route. Those figures are not equivalent landed prices and do not justify declaring one product better value.

Before ordering, resolve the label gaps and request the final total for each eligible address. The registered guides record different return periods: 60 days for SenFlo and 90 days for Integrative, with postage details needing confirmation. Persistent symptoms or frequent laxative needs belong in a conversation with a qualified professional.

verdict: These are different digestive proposals with different information gaps. Request SenFlo's quantitative panel first; ask for individual amounts and enzyme activity detail for Integrative. Neither the category label nor the pack-day marketing supports substitution or combined use.
checks: Request the full current SenFlo panel and senna amount.
Do not treat package days as a laxative-use course.
Ask for enzyme activity units and individual blend amounts where relevant.
Compare eligible destinations and full delivered totals separately.
audience: Adults comparing supplement labels, serving definitions and purchase conditions

title: EZNaturals Moringa vs Pep Tonic: Capsule & Powder Comparison
question: Capsule or mixed drink?
description: EZNaturals Moringa vs Pep Tonic: compare a capsule with a mixed powder, extract statements, fibre and blend disclosure. US and UK purchase conditions are kept separate.
lead: EZNaturals Moringa and Pep Tonic can both attract adults browsing plant-based nutrition products. One combines moringa powder and extracts in a capsule; the other is a mixed drink with fibre and several compounds. The formats and market routes need separate comparisons.
rows: One vegetable capsule; 60 servings per bottle
One 10 g scoop; 30 servings per container
100 mg moringa powder; 20 mg 10:1 extract; 235 mg 20:1 extract
5 g dietary fibre, 1 g protein and multiple compounds and blends
Rice flour, vegetable cellulose and magnesium stearate
CoQ10 100 mg, beta-NMN 300 mg, PQQ 20 mg, among other entries
Extract ratios do not independently establish potency or outcomes
Individual amounts within fibre and superfood blends are undisclosed
US$69 before destination charges, 10 October snapshot
US$59.95 before destination charges, 7 October snapshot
US-targeted Moringa offer; UK delivery not established
UK-listed Pep Tonic route; confirm exact address and charges

sections.title: Do not convert the capsule into an imaginary scoop equivalent
paragraphs: Moringa's three entries describe leaf powder and two extracts. The 10:1 and 20:1 ratios are supplier ingredient descriptions, not evidence that a capsule supplies a particular serving of whole vegetables. Adding extrapolated raw-leaf equivalents would hide assumptions that have not been verified here.

Pep Tonic's 10 g scoop includes fibre and several separately stated compounds alongside two blends. Its green-drink presentation is therefore not equivalent to a single-plant capsule. Neither format establishes nutritional equivalence to a balanced diet or a finished-product energy benefit.

sections.title: Compare practical preferences with the full composition
paragraphs: The capsule may be simpler to carry, while the powder requires measuring and mixing. Those are format observations, not claims of better adherence or absorption. Preferences about flavour, sweeteners and capsule materials should be checked against the actual ingredients rather than inferred from the product category.

Moringa's label includes a facility statement about common allergens. Pep Tonic includes flavouring, acids and stevia as well as its botanical and other compounds. Ask a qualified professional about the full formula, especially with medication, pregnancy, nursing or an existing condition. Do not assume that plant-based means suitable for everyone.

sections.title: Supply labels and delivery claims need a second look
paragraphs: Moringa's bottle has 60 one-capsule servings, while the commercial 30-day description reflects a different assumed frequency. Its published one-to-two-times-daily wording explains that arithmetic; it is not a personal schedule we recommend. Pep Tonic has 30 labelled scoops, which is a different quantity measure.

The registered offers target different markets. The Moringa guide records a US checkout example with tax; the Pep Tonic guide discusses UK availability and possible destination costs. Compare current delivered totals only after confirming that both routes serve your address. Their 60- and 90-day guarantee descriptions also have different conditions and postage uncertainties.

verdict: Moringa offers a more focused botanical composition in a capsule. Pep Tonic provides a broader mixed-drink formula with fibre and undisclosed within-blend amounts. The right comparison concerns the complete ingredients, preferred format and available buying route; neither is established as a replacement for food.
checks: Keep powder, extract ratios and scoop weight as separate measures.
Read the full ingredient and allergen information.
Do not infer a personal schedule from commercial supply days.
Check whether both offers serve your address before comparing delivered cost.
audience: Adults comparing supplement labels, serving definitions and purchase conditions

market: AGE+ US only; Mitochondrial UK/Ireland offer; availability differs
title: SelfPlus AGE+ vs Advanced Mitochondrial Formula: Label Scope
question: One extract or a wider blend?
description: SelfPlus AGE+ vs Advanced Mitochondrial Formula: compare extract standardisation, trans-resveratrol amounts, formula breadth and different US/UK purchasing routes.
lead: SelfPlus AGE+ and Advanced Mitochondrial Formula share healthy-ageing and cellular-wellness marketing. Their labels describe different scopes: a focused resveratrol extract and a wider multi-ingredient formula. This review compares those facts without claiming a longevity result.
rows: 250 mg Japanese knotweed extract standardized to 50%, supplying 125 mg trans-resveratrol
Read the capsule materials and complete excipient list
CoQ10 50 mg, D-ribose 250 mg, niacinamide 200 mg, magnesium 45 mg and other entries
125 mg is part of the 250 mg extract, not an extra amount
Eleven declared amounts do not establish a superior finished product
US$79 plus advertised US$9.99 shipping, 24 October snapshot
US$79.95 before destination charges, 6 October snapshot
Registered UK/Ireland offer; no common destination assumed

sections.title: Compare the named compound rather than the extract headline
paragraphs: AGE+'s 250 mg extract is standardized to supply 125 mg trans-resveratrol. Those are nested quantities: adding them would count the constituent twice. The Mitochondrial panel separately lists 25 mg trans-resveratrol within a wider formula and defines a two-capsule serving.

The differing stated amounts identify a composition difference. They do not prove that more trans-resveratrol produces a better health outcome, or that either formula extends life. A supplier's research links about an ingredient are not automatically clinical evidence for the finished bottle.

sections.title: A broader formula also broadens the comparison
paragraphs: Advanced Mitochondrial Formula names CoQ10, D-ribose, niacinamide, magnesium and several botanical or other compounds. AGE+ centres on one extract, while still listing capsule materials and excipients. A focused formula is not the same as literally having no other ingredients.

For readers already using supplements, comparing overlap across the complete labels is more useful than choosing by ingredient count. Do not create a stack from a shared healthy-ageing theme. Suitability and medication interactions should be reviewed with a qualified health professional using the actual current panels.

sections.title: The apparent entry-price similarity hides market differences
paragraphs: The recorded single-bottle figures are close, but AGE+'s supplier policy lists US-only delivery and an advertised US$9.99 charge for the smaller packs. The initial checkout instead showed zero shipping. The Mitochondrial guide records a UK-selected three-bottle order. None is a matching final quote for the same address.

The registered AGE+ policy describes a 60-day request period and customer-paid change-of-mind return postage. Mitochondrial's inspected checkout describes 90 days and customer-paid return postage. Confirm the governing order policy and original-shipping treatment. A longer guarantee is a purchasing condition, not evidence of longer life or better energy.

verdict: AGE+ is a focused extract-based label; Advanced Mitochondrial Formula is a broader combination with a smaller declared trans-resveratrol amount per label serving. Compare overlap and eligibility before price. The available material does not identify a clinical winner for longevity or fatigue.
checks: Do not add 125 mg trans-resveratrol to its parent 250 mg extract.
Compare complete formulas and existing supplement overlap.
Confirm that a suitable buying route serves your country.
Obtain the final shipping quote and order-specific return terms.
